ol.title: Run AI models on your own machine
ol.desc: Ollama runs open-weight models (Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek...) fully offline, free, with no request limits. Javis talks to it over the network, so the machine running Ollama does not have to be the one running Javis.
ol.note_native: Javis is running directly on this machine, so installing Ollama right here is enough.
ol.note_docker: Javis is running inside Docker, so "this machine" is the container, not yours. Install Ollama on YOUR real machine and put its address in the field below (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:11434).

ol.specs_title: Specs of the machine running Ollama

ol.specs_hint: What you enter wins over what Javis reads, even when Ollama runs on this very machine.

ol.dk_title: Three steps, on the SERVER itself, not in Javis's terminal
ol.dk_b1: SSH into the VPS as root. Javis's own terminal will not do: it runs inside the container, has no root, and anything installed there is wiped on the next update.
ol.dk_b3: Make Ollama listen on the Docker bridge address. Only containers on this host can reach it and nothing is exposed to the Internet, so no firewall step is needed:
ol.dk_b4: The address is already filled in below - just press Connect:
ol.dk_canh_bao: The command above binds Ollama to an internal address, so no firewall is needed. Only if you must use OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 (unusual Docker network) does Ollama listen to the whole Internet, and it has NO password: run ufw allow from THE-BRIDGE-SUBNET to any port 11434 then ufw deny 11434, or block port 11434 in your VPS provider's firewall.
ol.dk_cham: A VPS usually has no GPU and little RAM, so a CPU-bound model will be very slow. Your desktop at home (with a GPU, ideally) is the better host, at the cost of the VPS having to reach it.
ol.dk_khong_do_duoc: Javis could not work out the host address. Run the command below on the host, then put the number that follows the word default into the box above, with :11434 after it.
ol.dk_chan_doan: Still not connecting? On the host run: ss -ltnp | grep 11434. No line means Ollama is not running (see systemctl status ollama). A line with 127.0.0.1 means step 3 has not been done.
ol.set_main_ok: {ten} is now the main model. The model bar under the chat box has switched.
ol.canh_bao_cong_khai: Connected, but this is a public Internet address and Ollama has NO password, so anyone who knows it can use your models. Firewall port 11434 so only the Javis server can reach it.
ol.embed_note: Embedding model: makes search vectors, cannot answer. Javis has no use for this type yet.

cs.bk_media_head: By default only TEXT is synced, never media.
cs.bk_media_a: What goes to GitHub is notes, Wiki pages, memories, skills, recurring-job settings and scripts - that is, text files
cs.bk_media_b: Images, video, audio, PDFs and other binary files do NOT go up
cs.bk_media_c: they stay on this machine and work as usual, they simply never enter git history. Small IMAGES can be switched on with "Sync images too" below, once you have read the trade-off.
cs.bk_media_f: . A video file, once committed, sits there forever; deleting it later never wins the space back, and every re-export of the clip adds a whole new copy. A few hundred MB of media plus a habit of re-rendering will push the repo to several GB within months, and a fresh clone has to download even the versions you dropped long ago. Text is the opposite: git compresses it and stores only the difference, so a hundred edits stay tiny.

store.err.title: Could not install
store.confirm.title: Are you sure?
store.inspect.sha_note: If it matches the checksum the publisher announced, the file is the original - nobody edited it on the way.
store.inspect.conn_note: Every service from a pack starts at Read only. To allow writing, you raise the permission on each account yourself.
store.inspect.vault_note: If the brain already has an item with the same name, Javis keeps yours and skips the one in the pack. Uninstalling only deletes what you have not edited.
store.inspect.author: by {ten}
store.inspect.already.title: This machine already has this pack
store.inspect.already.body: Currently running {ver}. Installing again REPLACES the old version.
store.inspect.skipped.title: Part of the pack was skipped
store.inspect.community.title: Community pack
store.inspect.community.body: This pack was sent to the store by an outsider and has not been reviewed by the publisher. Read the part below carefully before installing.
store.inspect.code.title: This pack runs real Python inside the Javis server
store.inspect.code.body: It can read every API key, token and file Javis can read. There is no barrier at all. Only install packs from a source you trust.
store.inspect.enable.title: Turn on right after installing
store.inspect.enable.off_note: Off by default because the pack runs code, so you can look it over first.
store.inspect.enable.on_note: The pack is data only, so turning it on makes it usable right away.
store.inspect.type_wrong: You have to type the pack id exactly to install.
store.downloading.title: Downloading the pack
store.conn.sure: Are you sure you want to remove it?
store.conn.stop_body: {ten} stops working the moment you remove it. The connections are NOT deleted: install the service again and they keep running as before.
store.conn.gone_body: This service disappears from the Connections store and from every engine. Its files stay in the installation - Javis does not edit its own source - so you can install it again at any time.
store.installed_latest: Installed v{ver}, this is the latest
